adaptive_acquisition.cost_objective: expected source-standardized query loss plus lambda times cumulative normalized path-length, duration, and predicted-force cost
adaptive_acquisition.cumulative_risk: sum of registered source-predicted probe risk charges
adaptive_acquisition.first_reveal: reveal only the first selected probe response and reduce it to the registered geometry/force summary
adaptive_acquisition.first_stage: select one safe candidate using only source/calibration models, target initial geometry, registered query, and action descriptor; then seal its identity
adaptive_acquisition.logged_data_boundary: the two revealed responses come from separately recorded reset interactions; this is adaptive logged acquisition, not execution of a physical two-step sequence
adaptive_acquisition.second_reveal: reveal only the conditionally selected second probe response
adaptive_acquisition.second_stage: conditioned on the first response, either stop and predict or select one different safe probe from the remaining three; seal before reveal
adaptive_acquisition.stopping_rule: stop after zero or one probe whenever every safe remaining probe has nonpositive source-estimated net query value or violates the cumulative risk cap

baseline_contracts.dependence-destroyed-adaptive-two-probe: preserves first- and second-probe response marginals but permutes object-matched probe-to-drop dependence under a frozen source-only derangement
baseline_contracts.generic-information-adaptive-two-probe: same horizon, candidate library, costs and risk cap; maximizes source-estimated full latent information rather than registered-query value
baseline_contracts.source-fixed-two-probe-set: one unordered safe pair selected using source/calibration objects only and reused for every target object and both queries; both responses are always revealed
baseline_contracts.task-conditioned-best-single-probe: same source model, risk cap, query and candidate library as the adaptive policy; may reveal at most one response

claim_boundary: A positive result supports offline adaptive selection of at most two separately logged physical pokes for sealed cross-intervention drop queries.
The primary novelty claim requires superiority to both the best registered single-probe policy and a source-fixed two-probe set under matched risk and cost.

It does not establish online sequential probe execution, identical reset states, same-state counterfactual outcomes, unique material identification, calibrated full-state uncertainty, deployment safety, or closed-loop manipulation success.
If exact drop-outcome freshness cannot be established, the complete study is retrospective real-data mechanism evidence.

evidence_class.adaptive_acquisition: offline-selected reveal of at most two separately logged pokes

family_rules.rule: object_id contains Foam or equals Sponge or ToiletPaperRoll

primary_analysis.dependence_attribution_endpoint: fraction of adaptive gain over best-single-probe removed by the frozen object-matched dependence derangement
efficiency_endpoints: fraction of decisions stopping after zero, one, and two probes
primary_analysis.task_dependence_endpoint: fraction of target objects whose impact and settled queries induce different first probes or response-conditioned second-probe branches

components: final template-diagonal-normalized symmetric Chamfer distance to initial mesh

risk_and_cost.cost_weight: chosen once on calibration objects before target response access
risk_and_cost.cumulative_risk_cap: frozen on source and calibration objects before target response access

action_descriptor.boundary: isolated semantic slicer; byte-level carrier co-location is acknowledged and forbidden response fields are deleted before policy access
descriptor: tool location relative to the initial mesh

source_gate.failed_gate_behavior: stop before target first-probe selection or target drop access
required: for both registered queries, adaptive two-probe mean calibration loss is lower than no-probe
for both registered queries, adaptive two-probe mean calibration loss is lower than task-conditioned best-single-probe
adaptive two-probe cost-adjusted calibration loss is lower than source-fixed two-probe-set
adaptive two-probe cost-adjusted calibration loss is lower than generic-information adaptive two-probe
mean revealed probe count is strictly below two
at least two distinct branch-dependent second-probe identities occur across calibration folds
the impact and settled queries induce different acquisition trees for at least one calibration object
dependence destruction removes at least half of the adaptive advantage over best-single-probe
all unsafe probes are rejected and all nonpositive-value branches stop or return exact no-probe fallback

stages: exact historical exposure scan for every target drop take
source-object response and query model fitting
target action-descriptor slicing and first-probe selection
second selected-probe response reveal when selected
joint sealing of all target drop-query predictions
single target drop-outcome opening and scoring

take_roles.target_drop_rule: all complete dropping takes of each primary target object are held challenges

required: positive physical-object-mean raw query-loss gain versus no-probe
positive physical-object-mean raw query-loss gain versus task-conditioned best-single-probe
positive physical-object-mean cost-adjusted gain versus source-fixed two-probe-set
positive physical-object-mean cost-adjusted gain versus generic-information adaptive two-probe
all six target objects improve versus task-conditioned best-single-probe under the registered paired object loss
all six target objects improve versus source-fixed two-probe-set under the registered cost-adjusted paired object loss
the paired object-bootstrap 95 percent lower bound is positive versus best-single-probe and fixed-two-probe-set
the exact one-sided six-object sign probability is at most 0.015625 versus best-single-probe and fixed-two-probe-set
mean revealed probe count is strictly below two
stage two is used on at least 25 percent and at most 75 percent of target object-query decisions
at least three target objects exhibit branch-dependent second-probe selection
at least two target objects receive different acquisition trees for impact and settled queries
dependence destruction removes at least half of the adaptive advantage over best-single-probe
